_principle.notes: Switzerland applies the strictest principle in Europe: employers may process only data concerning the employee's suitability for the role or necessary for performance of the contract. Anything outside that is forbidden, and applicants have a recognised right to lie about forbidden questions.

pregnancy.legal_basis: OR Art. 328b; Gender Equality Act (GlG) Art. 3

religion.notes: Forbidden as a pre-hire question unless the employer is a tendency employer where the belief is job-essential.

health.notes: Permitted only for illnesses directly affecting job suitability.

genetic.legal_basis: Genetic Testing of Humans Act (GUMG) Art. 21
genetic.notes: Pre-symptomatic genetic testing in employment is flatly prohibited; results may not be requested even if a test was carried out for other reasons.

criminal_record.notes: Lawful only when directly job-essential (financial-sector executive, public-trust roles).

salary_history.notes: Not forbidden, but pay-equity case law (GlG) limits using it to justify lower pay for women.
